December: Shortest Days, Longest Memories

December is the shortest, coldest month for UK riding. The winter solstice brings barely 7.5 hours of daylight in Scotland. But December riding has its own quiet magic — frost-covered landscapes, empty roads, and the festive atmosphere of small-town Britain.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 2-7°C. Regular frost, occasional snow inland. Scotland frequently below zero.
  • Daylight: Sunrise 8am, sunset 3:45pm (shortest day). Under 8 hours of weak winter light.
  • Roads: Wet, often gritted, potentially icy. Black ice risk is at its highest.

December Riding Opportunities

  • Festive rides: Many bike groups organise Christmas runs — toy runs for charity, festive ride-outs, and Boxing Day meets.
  • Christmas markets: Ride to a nearby town's Christmas market for mulled wine (non-alcoholic, obviously) and festive atmosphere.
  • Winter landscapes: Frost-covered fields, bare trees against grey skies, and the occasional magical snow-on-hills day create landscapes of austere beauty.
  • New Year's Day ride: Starting the year on two wheels is a tradition for many riders. Plan a short, symbolic first ride.

Safety Priority

December riding demands maximum caution:

  • Ice is the number one hazard. If the temperature is below 3°C, assume there's ice somewhere.
  • Bridges and overpasses freeze first — approach with extra caution.
  • Ride only on main roads that are likely to be gritted.
  • If in doubt, don't ride. No ride is worth a crash on ice.

Bike Storage

If you choose not to ride through December, proper storage is essential:

  • Fill the tank to prevent condensation and rust inside
  • Connect a trickle charger to maintain battery health
  • Clean the bike thoroughly and apply corrosion protectant
  • Inflate tyres to recommended pressure to prevent flat spots
  • Cover with a breathable cover (not plastic — traps moisture)
Whether you ride or rest in December, stay connected to motorcycling. Clean your gear, plan next year's tours, browse maps, and dream of the long summer days ahead. The solstice is the turning point — from here, the days get longer.

Gift Ideas for Riders

December means Christmas shopping, and if you are buying for a motorcyclist or dropping hints for your own wish list, touring-specific gifts are always welcome. Heated gloves, a quality neck tube, a compact tank bag, a chain maintenance kit, and OS Maps subscriptions all make excellent practical presents for touring riders. For the rider who has everything, an experience gift like a track day voucher, an advanced riding course booking, or a ferry reservation for next summer's island tour creates anticipation that sustains through the dark winter months ahead.

Motorcycle-themed books are perfect winter reading material. Ted Simon's Jupiter's Travels, Robert Pirsig's Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance, and Sam Manicom's Into Africa are timeless classics that fuel wanderlust from the comfort of an armchair beside the fire. For UK-specific touring inspiration, look for route guidebooks covering Scotland's Highlands, the mountain passes of Wales, and England's most scenic national parks. faq.q: Is it safe to ride in December?
faq.a: December demands maximum caution because black-ice risk is at its highest. If the temperature is below 3C, assume there is ice somewhere, and remember that bridges and overpasses freeze first. Ride only on main roads that are likely to be gritted, and if in doubt, do not ride at all. No ride is worth a crash on ice, and daylight is limited to under 8 hours.

faq.q: What riding opportunities does December offer?
faq.a: December has its own quiet magic. Many bike groups organise Christmas runs, charity toy runs and Boxing Day meets. You can ride to a nearby Christmas market for the festive atmosphere, enjoy frost-covered landscapes of austere beauty, and take part in the New Year's Day first ride, a symbolic short outing to start the year on two wheels.

faq.q: How should I store my bike over December?
faq.a: If you choose not to ride, proper storage is essential. Fill the tank to prevent condensation and internal rust, connect a trickle charger to maintain battery health, clean the bike thoroughly and apply a corrosion protectant, and inflate tyres to the recommended pressure to prevent flat spots. Use a breathable cover rather than plastic, which traps moisture.

faq.q: What are good gifts for a motorcyclist in December?
faq.a: Touring-specific gifts are always welcome: heated gloves, a quality neck tube, a compact tank bag, a chain maintenance kit or an OS Maps subscription. For the rider who has everything, an experience gift such as a track day voucher, an advanced riding course or a ferry booking for next summer creates anticipation through the dark months. Motorcycle books make perfect winter reading.

faq.q: Why is the winter solstice significant for riders?
faq.a: The winter solstice is the turning point of the riding year. December brings barely 7.5 hours of daylight in Scotland and under 8 hours of weak winter light elsewhere, but from the solstice the days begin to lengthen again. Whether you ride or rest, it is a moment to stay connected to motorcycling by cleaning gear, planning next year's tours and dreaming of long summer days ahead.
